title: Co-op Readiness Dashboard for Teams
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: Co-op Readiness Dashboard for Teams
Thesis: A Power BI dashboard pinned in Microsoft Teams that maps a first-year student's CLR competencies against their target co-op track, with Copilot-generated weekly next-step nudges.
Why this frame: This is the textbook execution of the brief — a student-facing dashboard with red/green skill gaps, Copilot summaries, and an advisor cohort view. It honors Liz's cost-containment and no-new-platforms mandate by living entirely inside Power BI and Teams, and honors Jen's Copilot-integration mandate via Copilot for Power BI natural-language generation.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Maya Chen
  Role: First-year Khoury College student (Computer Science + Business combined major)
  Context: Five weeks into her first semester at Northeastern. She is staring down sophomore-year co-op recruiting and has heard that the strongest applicants started building portfolio-grade skills in their first year. She uses Microsoft Teams daily for class group chats and has noticed a new tab called 'My Co-op Readiness' pinned in her advising channel.
  Emotional state: Quietly anxious, ambitious, slightly overwhelmed by the menu of clubs, hackathons, research opportunities, and TA gigs — unsure which choices actually compound toward a target co-op.
  Pain points:
    - Cannot translate her course syllabi and club activities into the specific competencies a recruiter scans for.
    - Sees other students collecting badges and projects but has no benchmark for what 'enough' looks like by sophomore March.
    - Drowning in advice from upperclassmen, advisors, and parents — none of it indexed to her actual record.
    - Hesitant to bother her faculty advisor with what feels like a basic question: 'Am I on track?'
  JTBD: When I am deciding how to spend the 5–8 discretionary hours per week I have outside coursework, I want to know which single activity will most close the gap between my current CLR record and my target co-op track, so I arrive at sophomore recruiting season as a first-choice candidate.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Time-Constrained Faculty Advisor (Prof. Daniel Okafor): Opens the cohort heatmap once a week to spot students whose gap scores have stalled; uses the 'Students at Risk' default filter to triage outreach without manual roster review.
  - Liz, Director of Experiential Learning Operations: Approver and budget owner; reviews license utilization and the cost-zero deployment evidence; veto power on any feature requiring new procurement.
  - Jen, Director of Digital Transformation: Validates that Copilot integration is meaningful (not decorative) and that data flows stay inside the Microsoft 365 perimeter.
  - Microsoft-Aligned Technology Integrator: Maintains the CLR → Power BI dataflow, the daily batch sync job, and the Power Automate Teams digest.
  - Co-op Employer Liaison: Provides the competency baseline rubrics per co-op track (e.g., what 'Quantitative Analysis' means for a Fidelity data analyst role) that anchor the gap math.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Sunday evening planning ritual, 9:42 PM. Maya opens Microsoft Teams on her laptop, clicks the 'My Co-op Readiness' tab pinned to her Khoury First-Year channel, and sees four red competency tiles. Mid-session, her just-logged CLR record from Friday's Women in CS workshop syncs in — the 'Quantitative Analysis' tile flips amber-to-green in real time, Copilot's weekly brief rewrites itself, and Maya commits to two concrete actions for the week.

USE CASES (10) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Weekly Skill Gap Snapshot
     Trigger: Sunday 8 PM Power Automate digest pings Maya in Teams with 'Your week-6 readiness snapshot is ready.'
     Flow: Maya taps the deep-link → lands on the My Co-op Readiness tab → sees twelve competency tiles colored red/amber/green against her target track (Data Analyst Co-op) → scans the Copilot-generated headline → drills into one red tile to understand why.
     AI role: Copilot for Power BI composes a two-sentence natural-language summary of the dashboard state, surfaced above the tile grid.
     Outcome: Maya leaves the session with a clear mental model of her current standing — no advisor email required.
  2. Target Co-op Track Selector
     Trigger: Maya is debating whether her target track should be Data Analyst, Software Engineer, or Product Analyst.
     Flow: She opens the Track Comparison view → selects up to three tracks → the dashboard re-paints all twelve tiles three times, side-by-side → she sees that her current CLR record is closest to Product Analyst (4 reds vs 7 for SWE).
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro computes a Predictive Co-op Match Score per track using her CLR record + historical first-choice-placement data.
     Outcome: Maya rationally narrows her target track based on closest-fit, then revisits with her advisor for strategic confirmation.
  3. Two-Actions-This-Week Copilot Brief
     Trigger: Maya clicks the 'What should I do this week?' button in the Copilot panel.
     Flow: Copilot reads her top two largest gaps + her stated availability (5 hours/week) → suggests two concrete, time-boxed actions linked to specific Northeastern offerings → Maya can 'Add to my Outlook calendar' inline.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 (via the Copilot prompt surface) generates ranked, voice-matched recommendations with Verbalized Sampling — three alternative pairs with probabilities, Maya sees the top one and can request alternatives.
     Outcome: Maya commits to attending the Tuesday SQL Workshop and joining the Husky Data Club Friday meeting — both auto-scheduled.
  4. Real-Time Competency Sync from CLR
     Trigger: Maya logged her attendance at Friday's Women in CS Quant Workshop via the CLR mobile capture; the daily sync job at 9:30 PM Sunday picks it up.
     Flow: She is mid-session on the dashboard → a subtle 'Syncing CLR updates' banner appears → the Quantitative Analysis tile pulses, flips amber-to-green → the Copilot brief re-runs and updates the recommendations.
     AI role: Embeddings-based matcher tags the workshop's competency outcomes against her target track's rubric.
     Outcome: The classic 'aha' — Maya feels the system working with her, not at her.
  5. Activity-to-Competency Recommender
     Trigger: Maya clicks a red 'Stakeholder Communication' tile and asks 'How do I close this gap?'
     Flow: A modal opens listing seven Northeastern activities (clubs, courses, workshops, TA roles) ranked by competency-density for that specific gap, each with time commitment and badge yield.
     AI role: Wiki RAG over Northeastern's club and course catalog + Gemini 3.1 Pro ranking by competency match.
     Outcome: Maya joins the Husky Consulting Group based on a transparent 'closes 3 of your 4 reds' rationale.
  6. Advisor Cohort Heatmap
     Trigger: Prof. Okafor opens the same Teams tab from his advisor view on Monday morning.
     Flow: He sees a 38-row × 12-column heatmap of his advisees → the view defaults to 'Students at Risk' (sorted by lowest gap-closure velocity) → he clicks Maya's row to see her current state and message her directly in Teams.
     AI role: Cohort Anomaly Detection flags students whose gap-closure velocity has stalled for 14+ days.
     Outcome: Advisor triages outreach in under 5 minutes, replacing what used to be an hour of roster scanning.
  7. FERPA Consent & Visibility Controls
     Trigger: First-time access to the tab.
     Flow: Maya sees a clear consent banner explaining what CLR data is used, who can see her tiles (only her and her assigned advisor), and an opt-out for cohort-anonymized analytics.
     AI role: None — this is a deterministic compliance surface.
     Outcome: Trust is established before any data is shown; Liz's audit log captures the consent timestamp.
  8. Power Automate Weekly Teams Digest
     Trigger: Every Sunday at 8 PM, Power Automate triggers a personalized message in each student's Teams chat.
     Flow: The message reads: 'Hi Maya — 2 tiles changed this week. Your top action: attend Tuesday's SQL workshop.' → deep link opens the dashboard.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 composes the personalized one-liner using the latest dashboard state.
     Outcome: Mitigates the 'students ignoring the tab' risk; pushes the surface to them instead of waiting.
  9. Advisor One-Click Nudge
     Trigger: Prof. Okafor identifies three stalled students from the heatmap.
     Flow: He selects them → clicks 'Send encouragement nudge' → Copilot drafts three personalized Teams DMs referencing each student's specific largest gap → he reviews, edits one, sends all three.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 personalized drafting with advisor's voice preserved.
     Outcome: Outreach that used to be skipped now happens in 90 seconds.
  10. End-of-Semester Reflection Export
     Trigger: December, Maya wants to use her gap-closure story in a co-op application essay.
     Flow: She clicks 'Export my growth story' → receives a one-page PDF summary of competencies gained, activities completed, and trajectory chart → saved to her OneDrive.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 synthesizes a narrative summary suitable for a resume bullet or essay paragraph.
     Outcome: Maya enters spring recruiting with a portable artifact of evidence-based growth.

KEY SCREENS (9) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Teams Tab — My Co-op Readiness (Student Home) — purpose: Single-glance answer to 'where am I, what's next?' for the first-year student.
     Primary element: 12-tile competency grid colored red/amber/green with hover-reveal definitions, plus a Copilot brief panel pinned top-right.
     Motion character: Tiles fade in staggered at 60ms intervals on first paint; pulse-and-flip animation when a tile changes state mid-session.
  2. Competency Detail Drill-Down — purpose: Explain why a single competency is red and what closes it.
     Primary element: Vertical timeline of all CLR records that count toward this competency, with target-bar showing the threshold for the chosen track.
     Motion character: Timeline draws left-to-right on entry; threshold bar gently breathes to draw attention.
  3. Copilot Weekly Brief Panel — purpose: Surface the two-actions recommendation with Verbalized Sampling alternatives.
     Primary element: Conversational card with the top recommendation, 'Show alternatives' link revealing 2 more ranked options with probability badges.
     Motion character: Card content cross-fades when the underlying data changes; 'thinking' shimmer while generating.
  4. Track Comparison View — purpose: Help the student rationally pick a target co-op track.
     Primary element: Three-column side-by-side of the same 12-tile grid, with a 'closest fit' badge on the leading column.
     Motion character: Columns slide in left-to-right; the closest-fit badge bounces into place on render.
  5. Advisor Cohort Heatmap — purpose: Let Prof. Okafor triage his 38 advisees in under five minutes.
     Primary element: Sortable heatmap (rows = students, columns = competencies) with default filter 'Students at Risk' and a per-row velocity sparkline.
     Motion character: Hover-to-highlight row and column; click-to-zoom into individual student card with smooth scale transition.
  6. Activity Recommender Modal — purpose: Translate a gap into a concrete next-step.
     Primary element: Ranked list of Northeastern activities with competency-density bars and 'closes N of your reds' labels.
     Motion character: Modal blurs the background; recommendations animate in as a ranked list with rank-number popping.
  7. Sync Status & FERPA Footer — purpose: Continuous trust + transparency about data freshness.
     Primary element: Persistent footer strip: last-sync timestamp, FERPA consent state, 'view my data permissions' link.
     Motion character: Subtle pulse on the sync indicator when a batch lands; otherwise still.
  8. FERPA Consent Modal (first-run) — purpose: Establish trust before any data render.
     Primary element: Plain-language consent flow with three radio choices and a single 'I understand' button.
     Motion character: Slow fade-in, no flourish — gravitas.
  9. End-of-Semester Growth Story Export — purpose: Give the student a portable artifact.
     Primary element: Preview pane of the one-page PDF with the synthesized narrative and the gain-chart.
     Motion character: Page renders with a paper-fold animation; download button pulses when ready.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Copilot for Power BI Natural-Language Summary
     User action: Lands on the dashboard or refreshes after a sync.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Current 12-tile state (RAG/AMB/GREEN), target track rubric, last-week delta.
     Output: Two-sentence headline summarizing standing + the largest movement of the week.
     User benefit: Maya understands her dashboard in 4 seconds instead of 40, with no jargon.
  2. Two-Actions-This-Week Recommender (HEADLINE)
     User action: Clicks 'What should I do this week?' or receives the Sunday Teams digest.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7 with Verbalized Sampling
     Input: Ranked gap list, stated weekly availability, Northeastern activity catalog (via Wiki RAG), historical co-op match patterns.
     Output: Two concrete, time-boxed actions for the week, plus two alternative pairs each labeled with a probability of being chosen.
     User benefit: Maya converts vague anxiety into a calendar entry within 30 seconds.
  3. Competency Gap Ranking
     User action: Implicit on every dashboard load.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Student's CLR record, target track's competency thresholds, time-to-co-op window.
     Output: Ranked list of gaps weighted by impact-on-placement.
     User benefit: The 'red' tiles aren't just deficits — they're sorted by what will actually move the needle.
  4. Activity-to-Skill Matcher (Wiki RAG)
     User action: Opens the Activity Recommender Modal for a specific gap.
     Model: Wiki RAG over Northeastern club/course/workshop catalog + Embeddings
     Input: Target competency definition, full catalog corpus.
     Output: Top 7 activities with competency-density score and time-commitment estimate.
     User benefit: Maya gets transparent, evidence-backed recommendations instead of upperclassman folklore.
  5. Predictive Co-op Match Score
     User action: Compares two or three target tracks in the Track Comparison view.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Current CLR record, anonymized historical first-year-to-co-op trajectories, target track rubrics.
     Output: Probability of securing first-choice co-op in each track, with key drivers explained.
     User benefit: Track selection becomes a data-informed decision, not a coin flip.
  6. Cohort Anomaly Detection
     User action: Advisor opens the heatmap.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Cohort gap-closure velocities over the past 30 days.
     Output: Flagged list of students whose velocity has stalled or reversed, with suggested reason codes.
     User benefit: Advisor outreach goes from reactive to proactive without manual roster review.
  7. Advisor Nudge Drafter
     User action: Advisor selects students and clicks 'Send encouragement nudge'.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Each selected student's largest gap + recent activity, advisor's prior message tone samples.
     Output: Personalized DM drafts ready for one-click send.
     User benefit: Advisor sends thoughtful outreach in 90 seconds instead of skipping it entirely.
  8. Growth Story Synthesizer
     User action: Student clicks 'Export my growth story' at semester's end.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Full semester of CLR records, gap-closure trajectory, activities completed.
     Output: One-page narrative summary suitable for resume bullets or co-op essay openings.
     User benefit: Maya enters spring recruiting with a portable, evidence-based growth artifact.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Microsoft Fluent 2 inside Teams chrome, data-dense editorial restraint, traffic-light precision (Fluent red #C50F1F / amber #F7630C / green #107C10), institutional trust signals (Northeastern husky-red accent #C8102E used sparingly for primary CTA), generous whitespace around dense grids, monochrome charts with one accent color per view.
  Hero treatment: The dashboard itself is the hero — no decorative imagery. The grid of twelve traffic-light tiles is the visual signature, framed by the authentic Microsoft Teams left rail, top app bar, and tab strip. The Copilot brief panel uses the Fluent gradient sparkle icon and a soft lavender-tinted card background to subtly distinguish AI-generated text from system data, building the trust pattern Jen and Liz both endorsed.
  Motion character: Restrained, purposeful, Fluent-native. No bouncy delight on routine interactions — only the tile-flip on a real CLR sync earns the cubic-bezier overshoot. Hover states use 180ms ease-out lifts at 4px. Skeleton shimmers replace spinners. The single 'aha' moment (the tile flip) is intentionally the most expressive motion in the entire product — everything else is calm, fast, and confident.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Imagen prompt: 'Editorial illustration of a Northeastern University husky in Fluent 2 line-art style, sitting in a study carrel with a laptop showing a traffic-light grid, monochrome with a single red accent — used as the empty-state hero for first-time tab open.'
    2. Imagen prompt: 'Abstract data-flow diagram showing CLR database → secure API → Power BI dataset → Microsoft Teams tab, in Fluent isometric style, used in the FERPA consent modal as a trust-building diagram.'
    3. Imagen prompt: 'Photographic portrait of a diverse first-year college student in a co-working space, soft natural light, looking confidently at a laptop — used as the testimonial header on the advisor onboarding screen.'
    4. Imagen prompt: 'Minimal vector badge artwork: Quant Foundations Micro-Badge, Data Analyst Foundations, Consulting Practitioner Badge — Fluent geometric medallions in Northeastern red and Fluent neutrals.'
    5. Imagen prompt: 'Editorial cover illustration for the End-of-Semester Growth Story PDF — a stylized trajectory line rising left-to-right over a faded competency grid, husky-red accent line, used as the export PDF cover image.'

FEATURE ROADMAP (3 phases) — the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3) — Foundations — CLR-to-PowerBI Pipeline & Student Tab MVP
     • Map CLR data fields to the 25-competency taxonomy and 12 co-op-track rubrics.
     • Build the daily batch sync job from CLR DB → Power BI dataset via secure API.
     • Ship the My Co-op Readiness tab in Teams with the 12-tile competency grid and FERPA consent flow.
     • Implement Copilot for Power BI two-sentence summary at the top of the tab.
     • Deploy Sunday 8 PM Power Automate Teams digest to all first-year pilot students.
     Success: 100% of pilot cohort (38 students) has viewed their dashboard at least twice within the first three weeks; 70%+ open rate on the Sunday digest.
  2. Phase 2 (Month 2) — Intelligence — Recommender + Advisor Cohort View
     • Ship the Activity-to-Competency Recommender modal with Wiki RAG over the Northeastern catalog.
     • Launch the Two-Actions-This-Week Copilot brief with Verbalized Sampling alternatives.
     • Deliver the Advisor Cohort Heatmap with 'Students at Risk' default filter and velocity sparklines.
     • Implement Cohort Anomaly Detection flagging stalled gap-closure velocity.
     • Add the Advisor One-Click Nudge Drafter.
     Success: Advisor time spent explaining skill gaps drops 40%; 50%+ of students act on at least one Copilot recommendation per week.
  3. Phase 3 (Quarter 2) — Scale — Track Comparison, Growth Story, & Full Roll-Out
     • Launch the Track Comparison view with Predictive Co-op Match Score.
     • Ship End-of-Semester Growth Story Export to OneDrive PDF.
     • Expand from Khoury pilot to all first-year colleges (Khoury, D'Amore-McKim, COS, COE).
     • Add quarterly Liz-facing license utilization + cost-avoidance report.
     • Establish a feedback loop: dashboard interaction telemetry → quarterly rubric refinement with Co-op Employer Liaisons.
     • Publish accessibility audit and WCAG AA certification.
     Success: Student awareness of missing competencies up 60%; first-choice co-op placement rate up measurably among the cohort that used the tool weekly.

NARRATIVE ARC (8 beats) — the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1
     User: Maya clicks the new 'My Co-op Readiness' tab in her Khoury Teams channel for the first time. She reads a plain-language FERPA consent and accepts.
     AI: The system loads her CLR record, runs the gap ranking, and Copilot composes a calm two-sentence summary above twelve red/amber/green tiles.
     Feeling: Surprised relief — 'This is finally legible.'
  2. Minute 8
     User: Maya drills into a red Quantitative Analysis tile and opens the Activity Recommender. She joins Husky Data Club through the inline link.
     AI: Wiki RAG ranks seven activities by competency density; Copilot explains why the top one closes 3 of her 4 reds.
     Feeling: Capable — 'I know exactly what to do.'
  3. Day 1 (later that night)
     User: Maya screenshots her dashboard to send to her mom — first time she has confidently shown anyone her academic plan.
     AI: Background: telemetry logs the first activity-sign-up event for the cohort.
     Feeling: Proud, in control.
  4. Week 1
     User: Sunday 8:03 PM: Teams pings with her week-2 digest. The Quantitative Analysis tile is now amber. She commits to two more actions.
     AI: Power Automate fires the digest; Copilot composes a personalized headline referencing her movement.
     Feeling: Momentum — 'It noticed.'
  5. Week 4
     User: Mid-session, Maya watches the Quantitative Analysis tile flip amber-to-green as Friday's workshop syncs in. She gasps audibly.
     AI: Sync event triggers a tile re-render with a pulse-flip animation; Copilot brief rewrites in place.
     Feeling: Delight — the headline 'aha.'
  6. Month 1
     User: Prof. Okafor messages Maya in Teams referencing her growth: 'Saw your Quant tile turn green — let's talk Product Analyst tracks.'
     AI: Advisor used the One-Click Nudge Drafter; Copilot generated the personalized opener.
     Feeling: Seen — by a human, with data behind them.
  7. Month 3
     User: End of semester. Maya exports her Growth Story PDF and uses two lines verbatim in a winter externship application.
     AI: Claude synthesizes the trajectory into resume-grade prose; saves to OneDrive.
     Feeling: Equipped — she has a portable artifact of her own growth.
  8. Spring + sophomore recruiting
     User: Maya enters sophomore co-op recruiting with 9 green tiles, 2 amber, 1 red — and an evidence trail of how she got there.
     AI: Predictive Co-op Match Score now confidently places her in the top quintile for Product Analyst tracks.
     Feeling: Confidence rooted in evidence, not folklore.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (12 beats) — the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Maya opens Microsoft Teams on her laptop at 9:42 PM Sunday and clicks the 'My Co-op Readiness' pinned tab.
     System: Tab loads inside Teams chrome; the dashboard renders the persistent header 'My Co-op Readiness · Target Track: Data Analyst Co-op'.
     Motion/feedback: Soft top-down fade-in on header; subtle skeleton shimmer where tiles will land. (350ms)
  2. Maya's eye lands on the 12-tile grid.
     System: Tiles paint in staggered, top-left to bottom-right, each colored red/amber/green per current gap state.
     Motion/feedback: 60ms stagger between tiles; gentle scale-from-0.96 entrance. (850ms)
  3. Maya reads the Copilot brief panel pinned top-right.
     System: Brief reads: 'You closed one gap this week — Stakeholder Communication is now amber. Your largest remaining gap is Quantitative Analysis. Two suggested actions below.'
     Motion/feedback: Brief text types in at 30ms/char for the first sentence, then snaps for the rest. (1200ms)
  4. Maya scans down, sees four red tiles. Her cursor hovers on the Quantitative Analysis tile.
     System: Tile lifts 4px, casts a soft Fluent depth-2 shadow, reveals the threshold-vs-current bar at the tile bottom (3 of 6 evidence units).
     Motion/feedback: Lift transition 180ms ease-out; threshold bar fades in. (180ms)
  5. Before Maya clicks, the persistent footer pulses: 'CLR sync in progress — 1 new record.'
     System: Sync banner appears briefly center-top: 'Updating your dashboard with new activity.'
     Motion/feedback: Footer indicator pulses; banner slides down 24px, hangs for 1.2s. (200ms)
  6. Maya pauses, watching.
     System: Behind the scenes: the Friday Women in CS Quant Workshop record arrives, embeddings match it to Quantitative Analysis + SQL Fluency competencies, gap ranker re-runs.
     Motion/feedback: Quantitative Analysis tile begins a slow amber-glow. (600ms)
  7. Maya watches the tile.
     System: Quantitative Analysis tile executes the flip animation — red face rotates Y-axis 180° revealing the green face with the new threshold bar showing 6 of 6.
     Motion/feedback: Flip duration 700ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) — slight overshoot for delight. (700ms)
  8. Maya audibly reacts.
     System: Copilot brief cross-fades to new text: 'A new CLR record just synced — Quantitative Analysis is now green. Updated recommendations below.'
     Motion/feedback: 300ms cross-fade; small confetti-free Fluent 'spark' icon next to the changed sentence. (300ms)
  9. Maya scrolls to read the new Two-Actions-This-Week recommendations.
     System: Top recommendation: 'Join NUImpact Consulting Group — Wednesday 7 PM. Closes 3 of your remaining 3 reds in Stakeholder Communication and Leadership.' Secondary: 'Attend SQL Fluency Office Hours — Thursday 4 PM.'
     Motion/feedback: Each recommendation card slides up 8px and fades in at 80ms stagger. (400ms)
  10. Maya clicks 'Show alternatives' to see Verbalized Sampling options.
     System: Two alternative pairs reveal beneath, each tagged with probability badges (e.g., 'top pick · 62%', 'alt · 24%', 'alt · 14%').
     Motion/feedback: Accordion expands with 240ms ease-out; probability badges scale in. (240ms)
  11. Maya clicks 'Add to my Outlook calendar' on the top recommendation.
     System: Inline confirmation: 'Added — Wednesday 7 PM, NUImpact Consulting Group, Hayden Hall.'
     Motion/feedback: Button morphs to checkmark; confirmation toast slides in from bottom-right. (200ms)
  12. Maya closes Teams.
     System: Telemetry logs the gap-closure + action commitment; advisor cohort heatmap updates Maya's velocity sparkline for Monday morning.
     Motion/feedback: Silent server-side update; advisor will see the green movement at Monday 8:30 AM open.

=== CONSULTING BRIEF (every field below is mandatory grounding for the prototype) ===
Thesis: Visualizes missing competencies for first-year students to guide precise co-op preparation.
Description (what gets built):
A Power BI dashboard embedded directly within Microsoft Teams that aggregates a student's current Comprehensive Learner Record data against the baseline requirements of their desired co-op track. The dashboard highlights specific missing competencies in red and completed ones in green. First-year students view this weekly to understand exactly what they need to accomplish next. Advisors access a rolled-up view of their entire cohort to identify systemic skill gaps. The AI component uses Copilot to generate natural language summaries of the dashboard data, telling the student exactly which two actions to take this week to close the largest gaps.
Why it matters for first-year students:
First-year students often lack awareness of how their current coursework translates into tangible skills. By explicitly mapping their progress, this tool reduces the friction of guessing what employers want. This addresses the core issue of behavioral differentiation, focusing purely on what the first-year students have actually achieved and what they still need to do.
How it supports first-year students outcomes over first year before co-op placement:
By clarifying skill gaps early, first-year students can select projects that directly build required competencies. This leads to a higher percentage of students securing their first-choice co-op placements and reduces the time-to-placement metric during the active search cycle.
CLR dependency / independence rationale:
This concept relies entirely on the CLR infrastructure to supply the underlying competency data. It ingests the structured records of achievements and outputs a visual gap analysis based on that specific dataset. Without the CLR data feeds, the dashboard would have no baseline to measure against.
Execution within Northeastern University's existing stack (named systems, connectors, AI layer location):
The solution is built natively within Power BI and embedded as a tab in the existing Microsoft Teams environment used by students and advisors. Data flows from the CLR database into Power BI via secure APIs. Copilot for Power BI generates the text summaries. No external platforms or new portals are required, keeping the entire experience within the authenticated Microsoft perimeter.
Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Power Automate, Power BI fit (named tools that reduce cost/burden):
Utilizing Power BI and Teams eliminates the need for a separate student-facing web application. Microsoft Copilot handles the natural language generation natively. This approach honors the cost containment guardrail by maximizing existing enterprise licenses and avoiding third-party software procurement.
Key stakeholders:
  1. Liz — Approves the use of existing Power BI licenses to ensure zero new costs.

research_goal: Generate a slide-ready consulting report for NXT Humans, structured as an Executive Summary, Meeting Guardrails and Validation Criteria, Ideas to Retire or Reframe, Five CLR-Dependent Recommendations, Five Non-CLR Recommendations, Recommended Prioritization, and Suggested Next Steps for NXT Humans. This report must present 10 practical, AI-enabled recommendations for Northeastern University's first-year students to improve co-op and experiential learning readiness. Five recommendations must leverage CLR data and infrastructure, and five must be valuable independently of CLR. Each recommendation requires a title, description, rationale for first-year students and co-op readiness, explanation of CLR dependency/independence, execution within Northeastern's existing experiential learning stack, integration with Microsoft Copilot/365/Teams/SharePoint/Power Automate/Power BI for cost reduction, key stakeholders, implementation steps, risks, and explicit validation against Liz and Jen’s guardrails (cost containment, Microsoft ecosystem, no new platforms, advisor/student burden, AI-enabled, practical). The report should also summarize Liz and Jen’s priorities and non-starters, core design principles, and previous NXT Humans ideas to retire or reframe. Output the #recommendations #NU in this format, including tables comparing implementation complexity, student impact, Microsoft/Copilot fit, dependency, stakeholder burden, and strategic alignment.
